gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Kingbull Hunter 2.0S, a 26×4-inch fat-tire bike with a 750 W motor, sells for $949 on Kingbull's store today, or that adding Kingbull's $429 spare 18Ah pack makes $1,378 for two 18Ah packs (about 1,728 Wh). That costs less than ChatGPT's own budget pick, the Lectric XPeak 2.0 at about $1,500 with 720 Wh.
standout_why: Compared against bicyclingland.com (cited), sledgeback.com, electricbikeexplorer.com and fieldandstream.com. Bicyclingland skips the Kingbull bikes and prices the XPeak 2.0 at about $1,499. Sledgeback lists the Hunter 2.0S at $1,699 ($1,639 with a code) and the Ranger at $1,399. Electricbikeexplorer comes closest: it has the Hunter 2.0S at $999 with 864 Wh, a 150 lb rack and a 400 lb payload. But none of them gives today's $949, the $429 spare-pack price or the two-pack range-per-dollar math. Field & Stream has no Kingbull and prices an older Lectric X-Peak at $1,300. None of the four gives a noise measurement in dB for any bike.
decides: For 'budget + enough range to haul gear', this undercuts ChatGPT's budget pick. The Hunter 2.0S plus a spare pack is still $121 cheaper than the single-battery Lectric XPeak2 High-Step ($1,399 today), and it is $221 cheaper than the 960 Wh XPeak (listed at $1,599 on our page; I could not recheck that today). It also offers 150 lb of rack (electricbikeexplorer's figure) against the XPeak's 60 lb. That makes the Kingbull the price-and-range pick under $1,400. The Lectric stays the better-documented choice: Bicyclingland measured 24.6 mi with 1,541 ft of climbing on it, and no loaded range test exists for the Kingbull. Quietness can't decide between them because no page measured motor noise for either.

findings.label: Spare battery price
findings.value: $429 for the 18Ah pack (fits Ranger and Hunter 2.0S, 10.1 lb, charger not included)
findings.source_title: 18Ah Kingbull Battery Pack(Ranger and Hunter 2.0S Compatible)
findings.note: Bike plus spare = $949 + $429 = $1,378. Kingbull's charger for these models outputs 54.6 V, which means a 48 V nominal pack, so 48 V × 18 Ah = 864 Wh per pack and about 1,728 Wh for two. Electricbikeexplorer and Sledgeback also give 864 Wh. That works out to roughly $0.80 per Wh, against $1,399 / 720 Wh ≈ $1.94 per Wh for the XPeak2 High-Step.
